extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors, reviewers, and recommenders working on archaeology-related preprints (PCI Archaeology community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating and recommending archaeology-related preprints submitted to PCI Archaeology, covering eligibility, methodological and ethical standards, conflicts of interest, and equity/inclusion practices. Intended to direct authors, reviewers, and recommenders on what PCI Archaeology expects and how submissions are selected and handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: High scientific, methodological, and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology recommends only preprints that meet high scientific, methodological, and ethical standards regardless of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are based on the study's scientific quality, methodological rigor, and ethical acceptability rather than perceived impact or novelty alone. These standards apply to all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code, and analysis sharing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires authors to share data, code, and analysis scripts with reviewers upon submission and with readers after recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide underlying materials to facilitate review; after a positive recommendation these materials should be made available to readers. This is presented as a mandatory condition for evaluation and for providing citable validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Expects clear justification of sample sizes in empirical studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical submissions should include explicit rationale (e.g., power analysis, sampling rationale) for chosen sample sizes to allow assessment of robustness and validity of statistical inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to replications, preregistered research, and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes replications, preregistered research, and negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI explicitly encourages submission and positive evaluation of work that replicates previous findings, uses preregistration, or reports null/negative findings, treating these as valuable contributions rather than barriers to recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest policy for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not accept submissions with financial conflicts of interest; other conflicts must be minimal and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial conflicts disqualify submissions. Any non-financial conflicts must be declared and are expected to be minimal. This applies to authors and is mirrored by efforts to minimize conflicts among reviewers and recommenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest management for reviewers and recommenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensures, as much as possible, that reviewers and recommenders are free from conflicts of interest related to the study or its authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI takes steps to avoid assigning reviewers/recommenders who have conflicts with the submission; where unavoidable, conflicts should be declared and managed to preserve fairness of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender-interest prerequisite for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Only preprints that attract the interest of at least one recommender (similar to an associate editor) are sent for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders act as gatekeepers: they select work that stands out to them for its context, questions, methods, or findings. If no recommender expresses interest within 20 days, the submission is not considered for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria used by recommenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders select work that stands out (to them) for its context, questions, methods, or findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is subjective to recommender judgment but focuses on significance of context, clarity and importance of research questions, soundness/novelty of methods, and interest of findings. These are the aspects that prompt a submission to be sent to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and topical scope eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Archaeology will evaluate preprints written in English dealing with all fields of archaeology, anthropology, and human-environment interactions worldwide since the appearance of human cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible submissions must be in English and may span any discipline, method, or timeframe relevant to understanding the human past; interdisciplinary approaches that enhance knowledge about the human past are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to COPE and PCI code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Community In subscribes to the principles of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and has its own code of conduct that its users must comply with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants (authors, reviewers, recommenders, board members) are expected to follow COPE principles and the site's code of conduct; breaches may affect evaluation or participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and inclusion commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is attentive to equity and inclusion at all stages of the scientific article evaluation process and focuses on bringing more people who are underrepresented in academia among authors submitting to PCI, and on recruiting reviewers, recommenders, and Managing Board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommendations are given to reviewers, recommenders, and Managing Board members to increase equity and inclusiveness. Appointment and recruitment practices should consider underrepresentation linked to career stage, gender, and geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools to increase equity and inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibility to submit articles anonymously; transparency in the evaluation of articles; Managing Board members take into account underrepresentation when appointing new recommenders; template messages to recommenders and reviewers include recommendations about equity and inclusiveness; possibility to review anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational measures (anonymous submission/review, transparent evaluation, targeted appointment practices, and templated equity guidance) are provided to actively increase participation from underrepresented groups and reduce bias in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and public recommendation outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of positive evaluation, PCI Archaeology validates and publicly recommends those peer-reviewed preprints, providing citable documentation for the preprint's methodological rigour and the legitimacy of its results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A positive recommendation produces a public, citable statement attesting to methodological rigour and validity. Recommended preprints may be transferred to the diamond open-access Peer Community Journal or submitted elsewhere with this validation.
